messages:
maya: Hey team, checking in — today is my first day on infra. I never received the Okta activation link and Google Workspaces says 'not provisioned'. The onboarding doc's 1Password join link returns 403. Who should I ping to get these sorted?

it-ops-bot: Automation notice: No Okta activation found for maya@redwood.dev. If this is incorrect, please confirm your company email. Otherwise open a ticket in #it-ops or DM @sam.

sam: Welcome @maya! Sorry about the friction. Confirming: maya@redwood.dev? Also what OS are you on and do you need a laptop image?

maya: yep maya@redwood.dev. MacBook Pro (monterey). No laptop image needed, just need SSO + 1Password + repo access.

sam: Ok queued a resend of the Okta activation and kicked Google provisioning. You should see Okta email within a few mins. I also forwarded the 1Password 403 to eng-ops.

it-ops-bot: System: Okta activation resent to maya@redwood.dev (job 100221). Google sync job started.

maya: Got the Okta email and set my password, but when I click our SSO app in Chrome it spins and returns me to the Okta sign-in page (infinite redirect). Firefox works fine. Anyone seen this on Mac?

lee: Hey @maya — Chrome sometimes gets stuck because of blocked third-party cookies or an extension. Try chrome://settings/cookies -> Allow all cookies temporarily, or open an incognito window. Also disable any password manager autofill during first sign-in.

maya: Incognito worked, thanks! Now 1Password still gives 403 on the team invite URL when I try in the browser.

elaine: I added you to the infra vault just now. For CLI, run:

```bash
# sign in to 1Password CLI
eval "$(op signin --account redwood)"
op vault list | grep infra
```

If you still see 403, paste the sanitized error.

maya: CLI signin succeeded, can see infra vault. Browser link still 403 but CLI access is enough for now. Quick question on SSH: should I upload my public key to GitHub Enterprise personally or request the platform team to add it to the internal deploy manager?

devex: For developer access, add the SSH key to your GitHub Enterprise account and request org repo access in #eng-setup. For deploy keys (service accounts), file a ticket with eng-platform and include the public key.

maya: Added key to GitHub and requested org access. All set for now — appreciate the help! :tada:

sam: Awesome — welcome to Infra! Ping me or @devex if anything else pops up.
